location_assessment.name: Inaccessible Island
location_assessment.supported_finding: One named main island is appropriate as one location; the retained named-island coast comprises the relation's 12 outer ways.
location_assessment.unresolved_finding: Five separately closed coastline rings in the same retained OSM map extract lie outside the named-island relation and current location geometry. Their names, role and suitable treatment are not established.

source_geometry.current_published_geometry: Polygon with one exterior and one interior ring; the interior hole is mapped Skua Pond
source_geometry.point_in_polygon_check: Each closed way's vertex mean is outside the retained candidate land exterior. No area or independent location assignment is inferred from that test.

settlements_and_remainders.permanent_settlement: No evidence; UNESCO describes the island as uninhabited, and Tristan da Cunha government says it is rarely visited except by conservationists.
settlements_and_remainders.administrative_remainder: None identified. OSM relation 1974295 is tagged admin_level=4 but that community boundary tag does not establish an atlas tier or political owner.
settlements_and_remainders.ownership: Not inferred from GeoNames country/admin codes or OSM is_in tags. Current feature reference_owner is null.

location_assessment.temporal_limit: Modern source support only; no ancient shoreline, ownership, settlement history or attribute is inferred.
location_assessment.granularity_note: A named whole island is one subject irrespective of its source ring count. The nearby islet rings remain unresolved; EU5 scale counts are references, not quotas.

parent_assessments.name: Tristan da Cunha
parent_assessments.purpose_evidence: Official Tristan material identifies Inaccessible as an outer island of Tristan da Cunha; the parent is plausibly a whole-island-group geography.
parent_assessments.gap: Official Gough and Nightingale pages identify additional islands in this group, but no such current location is in the parent inventory.

parent_assessments.name: Tristan da Cunha
parent_assessments.purpose_evidence: Retained WGSRPD level-3 geographic reporting identity; the source's botanical groupings do not by themselves certify atlas tier purpose or complete membership.
parent_assessments.exception_candidate: One area containing one same-named province repeats a sparse-island grouping tier. Bouvet shows a parallel area/province repetition in the same region.
parent_assessments.gap: Complete island-family membership and the shared parents' semantic roles remain open.

neighboring_consistency.assessment: The region partitions into the Tristan da Cunha group and Bouvet Island. Both use a same-named province under an island-group area; this supports a candidate sparse-island repeated-tier exception, but does not close either semantic review.

proposed_follow_up.scope: Bounded complete source/membership audit for the Tristan da Cunha island family and the five nearby Inaccessible coastline rings.
proposed_follow_up.action: Verify authoritative source vintage/license/completeness, decide source-defined whole-land grouping at location granularity, propose exact members/crosswalks and request coordinated integration of both shared parents.
proposed_follow_up.do_not: Do not infer political ownership, change the shared hierarchy or boundary, or transfer historical attributes.
